cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tilted your head to judge that cupboard door, so I've tilted mine. It's still crooked. Give me the screwdriver.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm looking under the hinge for the screw I dropped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, underneath first. You find it; I'll take over the door while you're down there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. Hand me the screwdriver and I'll keep the door attached while you take the credit.

reason: Use concrete copied misunderstandings to shape control, quiet restoration, detail diversion, protective handling or inquiry, with each B contribution changing A's next move.
